reason: Both films share the same curb opening, overhead creek passage (13.0 to 17.7 s, frames identical), flood street, record cards, lot and closing split. They differ chiefly in the turn's first shot. A's side-view lane (28.4 to 32.6 s) shows the car with a lit red brake lamp at 30.6 s, the roadside slowing behind it and a standing-water patch on the same axis, then cuts at 32.8 s to the matching close side view where the front wheel enters the water (34.0 s), a wake forms and 'may' lights. The slow-then-roll mechanism reads at phone size. A's tabletop map (7.0 to 12.8 s) and desk record (22.2 to 24.4 s) also hold continuous perspective.
rejected_reason: B's overhead lane (28.4 to 32.6 s) draws the car at about an eighth of the frame width. Braking appears only as two tiny red marks from 30.8 s, the caption covers the lower half of the car at 28.6 s, and the car never reaches the water before the cut. The 'slow' of the recall sentence is much weaker at phone size, and the overhead-to-side cut at 32.8 s changes axis. B's other differences (overhead flat map 7.0 to 9.2 s, flat record cards) add no new information. B has no blocking defect; it is the weaker of two passing cuts.
